obligations.expected_behavior: For each terminal-selection case, invoke and exercise the actual public validator process.
forbidden_result: A substitute or non-public validator process is exercised.
obligations.observable_result: The case execution records that the public validator process was invoked and its result was obtained.
obligations.state_after: The actual public validator process has executed for the case.
obligations.state_before: A repository-owned terminal selection is ready to run a validator case.
obligations.subject: Repository-owned terminal selection
obligations.trigger: When a validator case is selected for terminal execution.

obligations.expected_behavior: Honor the selected mode when executing the validator case.
obligations.observable_result: The executed validator process and its behavior correspond to the requested mode.
obligations.state_after: The case has been executed under the requested mode.
obligations.state_before: A validator case includes a selected mode.
obligations.subject: Terminal validator selection
obligations.trigger: When a case is executed with a mode selection.

obligations.expected_behavior: Exercise CLI/API parity for valid, noncompliant, invocation-error, and legacy inputs.
forbidden_result: CLI and API diagnostics or outcomes are mismatched for any of the valid, noncompliant, invocation-error, or legacy inputs.
obligations.observable_result: For each of the four input classes—valid, noncompliant, invocation-error, and legacy—the CLI and API produce matching diagnostics and status semantics.
obligations.state_after: CLI/API parity has been asserted across all four input classes.
obligations.state_before: The validator is exercised through terminal and API paths for the defined input classes.
obligations.subject: CLI/API validator interfaces
obligations.trigger: When validating each valid, noncompliant, invocation-error, or legacy input.

obligations.expected_behavior: Assert fresh JSON output for every executed case.
forbidden_result: The case prints non-JSON output or extra output.
A stale or absent JSON result is accepted.
obligations.observable_result: Each case yields a newly produced JSON result with no non-JSON or extra output.
obligations.state_after: Fresh JSON output has been asserted for the case.
obligations.state_before: A validator case has produced terminal output.
obligations.subject: Terminal case output

obligations.expected_behavior: Assert the independently determined expected status for each case.
forbidden_result: A case is accepted without asserting its independent expected status.
obligations.observable_result: The actual status is compared with the independent expected status and the assertion result is recorded.
obligations.state_after: Independent expected-status verification is complete for the case.
obligations.state_before: The case has an independently determined expected status and an actual validator status.
obligations.subject: Validator case status assertion
obligations.trigger: After obtaining the actual status for each case.

obligations.expected_behavior: Assert that the process exit code matches the expected status for each case.
forbidden_result: The process returns exit code 0 for a fail, error, or legacy case.
The exit code does not match the expected status.
obligations.observable_result: Each case records a matching exit-code assertion, including fail, error, and legacy cases.
obligations.state_after: Exit-code matching has been asserted for the case.
obligations.state_before: The case has an expected status and an observed process exit code.
obligations.subject: Validator process exit code

obligations.expected_behavior: Use the existing CER/Q7/Q8 mechanisms for required case execution, skip, and error closure, without adding another test-runner or evidence writer.
forbidden_result: A separate test-runner is implemented for this closure.
A separate evidence writer is implemented for this closure.
obligations.observable_result: Case execution, skip, and error closure is delegated to the existing CER/Q7/Q8 mechanisms and no duplicate runner or evidence writer is introduced.
obligations.state_after: Required case closure is handled by the existing CER/Q7/Q8 mechanisms.
obligations.state_before: Existing CER/Q7/Q8 mechanisms own case execution, skip, and error closure.
obligations.subject: Case closure ownership
obligations.trigger: When implementing or wiring required case execution, skip, or error closure.
